message.content:
# Finding ∫ -2·exp(x)·cos(x) dx

## Step 1: Find ∫ exp(x)·cos(x) dx using integration by parts

Let I = ∫ exp(x)·cos(x) dx

**First integration by parts:**
- u = cos(x), dv = exp(x) dx
- du = -sin(x) dx, v = exp(x)

$$I = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x) + \int \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x)\, dx$$

**Second integration by parts** on ∫ exp(x)·sin(x) dx:
- u = sin(x), dv = exp(x) dx
- du = cos(x) dx, v = exp(x)

$$\int \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x)\, dx = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x) - \int \text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x)\, dx = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x) - I$$

## Step 2: Solve for I

$$I = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x) + \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x) - I$$

$$2I = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x) + \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x)$$

$$I = \frac{\text{exp}(x)\cdot(\cos(x) + \sin(x))}{2}$$

## Step 3: Multiply by -2

$$\int -2\cdot\text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x)\, dx = -2 \cdot \frac{\text{exp}(x)\cdot(\cos(x) + \sin(x))}{2}$$

$$= -\text{exp}(x)\cdot(\cos(x) + \sin(x)) + C$$

## Verification

$$\frac{d}{dx}\left[-\text{exp}(x)(\cos(x)+\sin(x))\right] = -\text{exp}(x)(\cos(x)+\sin(x)) - \text{exp}(x)(-\sin(x)+\cos(x))$$
$$= -2\text{exp}(x)\cos(x) \checkmark$$

<answer>-exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x)) + C</answer>
